newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish electricity protocol divides up sunk costs.
newsitem.headline: Spanish electricity protocol divides up sunk costs.

text.p: A new Spanish electricity protocol signed on Wednesday in an effort to liberalise the sector recognises total sunk costs of 1.99 trillion pesetas.
Sunk or stranded costs are fixed costs in plant and generation which in general will no longer be compensated by the state under the new more competitive regime.

Industry Minister Josep Pique said on Wednesday the 1.99 trillion peseta figure includes 300 billion as incentives for coal. A further 200 billion pesetas will correspond to compensation for extraordinary investments.
Total costs recognised to adapt to competition will be 1.5 trillion, Pique said.
Electricity companies will be allowed to pass on these costs via tariffs over the next 10 years, Pique said at the weekend.

Pique said at a news conference after the signing of the new framework that 75.4 percent of the costs would be divided up among the electricity companies as follows (in billions of pesetas unless otherwise stated):

The government was prepared to recognise 91.5 billion pesetas of sunk costs for Hidroelectrica del Cantabrico but the company refused to sign the accord at the last minute and thereby forfeited its share, Pique said.
"Because they didn't sign the protocol, Hidro-Cantabrico's part is zero," Pique said.
The allocation of the remaining 24.6 percent of the costs will be determined by work groups to be set up to study the issue.
